metadata.title: [FIX][API]: Add runtime `servers.use` compensation for pre-existing API tokens
metadata.author: madhav165

description:
# Bug-fix PR

---

## Summary
API tokens generated before the `servers.use` auto-injection fix (PR #3442) are rejected with HTTP 403 on `/rpc`, `/mcp`, and `/sse` transport endpoints, despite carrying valid MCP method permissions (`tools.read`, `tools.execute`, etc.).

This PR adds runtime compensation in the token scoping middleware so pre-existing tokens work without requiring rotation.

Closes #3451

## Reproduction Steps

1. Use an API token generated before commit `dbc43bb24` with permissions `["servers.create", "servers.read", "servers.update", "servers.delete", "gateways.read", "tools.read", "tools.execute"]`.
2. `POST /rpc` with a valid JSON-RPC payload (e.g., `tools/call`).
3. Observe HTTP 403 — `servers.use` is missing from the token's `scopes.permissions`.

## Root Cause
The auto-injection in `token_catalog_service._generate_token()` only runs at **token generation time**. Pre-existing long-lived API tokens were never updated, so they lack `servers.use`. The `token_scoping_middleware` blocks them at the transport layer before the RPC handler can enforce fine-grained per-method RBAC.

## Fix Description
Added runtime compensation in `_check_permission_restrictions()` (`mcpgateway/middleware/token_scoping.py`):

- When the required permission is `servers.use` and the token carries any MCP method permission (`tools.*`, `resources.*`, `prompts.*`), implicitly grant transport access.
- Mirrors the generation-time injection logic for pre-existing tokens.
- Non-MCP permissions (`gateways.*`, `servers.*`, `admin.*`, `llm.*`) do **not** get implicit transport access.

## Verification

| Check                                 | Command              | Status |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Lint suite                            | `make lint`          | -      |
| Unit tests                            | `uv run pytest`      | pass   |
| Coverage >= 80 %                      | `make coverage`      | -      |
| Manual regression no longer fails     | Pre-fix token now works on /rpc, /mcp, /sse | pass |

## MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

## Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

## Test Coverage
152 new parametrized tests in `TestRuntimeMcpTransportCompensation`:
- All 13 MCP permissions x 8 transport endpoints (104 allow-path tests)
- 10 non-MCP permissions x 4 transport endpoints (40 deny-path tests)
- Mixed permission lists, explicit `servers.use`, wildcard/empty edge cases
- Exact pre-fix and post-fix token scenarios
- Verification that compensation does not bleed into non-transport endpoints

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Rebased onto main (merge commit removed, 2 clean commits).

**Code review — approved.** The runtime `servers.use` compensation logic is correct, secure, and consistent with the generation-time injection in `token_catalog_service._generate_token()`:

- Compensation is properly scoped — only fires when `required_permission == Permissions.SERVERS_USE` (the 8 transport endpoints), does not leak to non-transport paths.
- Downstream per-method RBAC (`_ensure_rpc_permission()`) still enforces fine-grained permissions, so transport access alone doesn't widen what a token can do.
- `Permissions.MCP_METHOD_PREFIXES` constant is a good DRY improvement — single source of truth for both generation-time and runtime paths.
- 152 new parametrized tests provide thorough coverage: all 13 MCP permissions × 8 transport endpoints, 10 non-MCP deny paths, mixed permission lists, edge cases, and the exact pre-fix token scenario.
- All 1198 related tests pass, zero regressions.

commits.message:
fix(auth): runtime servers.use compensation for pre-existing API tokens

API tokens generated before the servers.use auto-injection fix lack
the servers.use transport permission, causing 403 on /rpc, /mcp, and
/sse endpoints despite having valid MCP method permissions.

Add runtime compensation in the token scoping middleware: when the
required permission is servers.use and the token carries any MCP
method permission (tools.*, resources.*, prompts.*), implicitly grant
transport access. This mirrors the generation-time auto-injection
from _generate_token() and ensures pre-existing tokens work without
requiring rotation.

Includes 152 new parametrized tests covering all MCP permission
prefixes across all transport endpoints, deny paths for non-MCP
permissions, mixed permission lists, and the exact pre-fix token
scenario.

Signed-off-by: Madhav Kandukuri <madhav165@gmail.com>

refactor(auth): extract MCP_METHOD_PREFIXES constant and add compensation logging

- Extract duplicated ("tools.", "resources.", "prompts.") tuple to
  Permissions.MCP_METHOD_PREFIXES in mcpgateway/db.py as single
  source of truth.
- Update token_scoping middleware and token_catalog_service to
  reference the shared constant.
- Add debug-level log when runtime servers.use compensation fires,
  helping operators identify tokens that should be rotated.
